title: The Premium Dilemma: Structuring your Heavy Hitters
dek: Haaland sits at 68.9% ownership. Owning the field's premium is a decision either way — here is what the numbers say about structuring around them.
body:
## The problem with premiums

A premium forward at £15m is not competing with the other forwards. He is competing with the two mid-price players you could field instead. That is the whole calculation, and it is worth doing with numbers rather than instinct.

## Where the money is going

| Player | Team | Price | Owned | Points | xGI | Mins |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Haaland | MCI | £15.5m | 68.9% | **2** | 0.76 | 90 |
| B.Fernandes | MUN | £12.0m | 50.6% | **2** | 0.34 | 90 |
| Isak | LIV | £9.0m | 17% | **2** | 1.1 | 90 |
| Palmer | CHE | £9.5m | 10.8% | **5** | 0.2 | 28 |

On points per million so far, **Palmer** leads this group at 0.53. **Haaland** is the most-owned at 68.9%, which makes him the one you are effectively forced to have an opinion about: not owning him is an active bet against 68.9% of the field.

> With 1 gameweek played, these totals are a starting position rather than a verdict. Points per million on a sample this small mostly measures who has had the kinder fixture.

## How to structure it

- **One premium, spread elsewhere.** Frees roughly £5m across two mid-price slots. Works when the mid-price bracket is deep.
- **Two premiums.** Forces genuine budget players into your defence. Viable when the cheap defenders are playing 90 minutes.
- **None.** Rarely correct, because the highest-owned premium sets the template score you are measured against.
source: Generated from current prices, ownership and season totals
